verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Four of the six frozen SHOULD-FIX items are closed outright and the fifth and sixth are closed in substance. The binding location is decided in the direction I asked and with the collision I flagged handled explicitly: verifiedInstallRoot is a signed carrier field, not a selector member, not part of completePlatformProfileKey, not an inventoryFieldAuthor entry, and coexistence states that inventoryFieldAuthor remains the single author of inventory bytes. The tree-root serialization is closed — token '/', every other value strictly relative with no leading slash and no empty, dot or dot-dot components, and an explicit join rule against the host anchor before canonicalization. observerProcessIdentity becomes the closed pair {pid, starttime} on both platforms with mandatory before-and-after verification around the read, Linux mountNamespaceIdentity becomes the /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt inode bound to that pair with inode equality, and macOS declares the field absent with no inapplicable token. Six retained fields plus an extended evidenceJoin now make the exact-volume comparison and the Linux retargeting check checkable from the trace. What holds acceptance is two things. The new signed carrier field is asserted onto a carrier whose own structural description was left byte-identical and unrostered, so no author, ceremony or binding point exists for it — the same gap PTCB-V3-S1 raised about the inventory field. And the starttime source is cited as '/proc/<pid>/stat field 22', a bare numeric ordinal on the one procfs file whose second field can contain spaces and parentheses, in a contract that forbids exactly that citation style for the mountinfo token.

shouldFix.title: verifiedInstallRoot is declared a signed carrier field, but the carrier block that defines the carrier was left unchanged and unrostered, so the field has no author, ceremony or binding point

measurement.whatLanded: My CLAUDE-V10-S1 asked the artifact to pick one of the two locations and to say how the choice coexists with the single-author rule. It does both. location reads 'signed carrier field verifiedInstallRoot. Not a platformProfile selector member. Not part of completePlatformProfileKey. Not an inventoryFieldAuthor inventory entry.' coexistence reads 'inventoryFieldAuthor remains the single author of inventory bytes. verifiedInstallRoot is a preselection carrier input, not inventory.' scope drops the slash entirely. That is the repair.
measurement.whatDidNot: /tcbCarrier is byte-identical to v10 and is not on the v11 roster. It still describes the carrier as 'The published signed-closure inventory. Exactly one copy', names exactly one author for exactly one field ('The DR-101 successor … authors the inventorySchema TCB / layer-table field'), gives bindingPoint as 'inventorySchema TCB members keyed by complete platformProfile. The field does not exist until that one DR-101 successor authors it', and routes signing to the OD-101-2 ceremony. The token verifiedInstallRoot does not occur anywhere in tcbCarrier.
measurement.theConsequence: A second class of field is asserted onto the one signed carrier with nothing saying who authors it, when it comes into existence, or where it binds. inventoryFieldAuthor is scoped to inventory bytes and coexistence expressly puts this field outside inventory, so that author does not cover it; signatureCeremonyOwner covers the ceremony, not authorship; and dependencyIfCarrierAbsent speaks only of the inventory carrier. signedBinding.absentDependency does handle the absent-value case by refusing, so the failure path is closed — what is open is provenance.

shouldFix.lineagePrecedent: PTCB-V3-S1 was raised on precisely this shape: a carrier field that did not yet exist and whose ownership was unclear. The repair then was to name one author, separate the ceremony, and state the carrier-absent consequence, and tcbCarrier still carries that text. The same three questions are unanswered for the field this generation adds. The artifact's own established remedy in this lineage is also on record: at v10 and v11 it repaired 'named but not provisioned' by adding the field to the structure that defines the container and putting that block on the roster — companionObservation into retainedEventSchema with /loaderTraces rostered, then the six volume fields the same way. /tcbCarrier was not given that treatment.
shouldFix.consequence: Fail-closed, not exploitable: with no value the profile refuses. But a signed input with no named author cannot be produced by anyone in particular, and the carrier's own description contradicts the claim that it holds this field.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Amend tcbCarrier to admit verifiedInstallRoot as a non-inventory preselection field, name its author and its relation to the OD-101-2 ceremony, and state when it comes into existence relative to dependencyIfCarrierAbsent. Put /tcbCarrier on that successor's roster.

shouldFix.title: starttime is cited as '/proc/<pid>/stat field 22', the bare numeric ordinal this contract forbids elsewhere, on the one procfs file where positional splitting is unsafe

measurement.theText: Both places read 'starttime = /proc/<pid>/stat field 22'. The token 'field 22' occurs twice; the artifact contains no rule for parsing that file, and the words comm and parenthesis do not appear in any parsing context.
measurement.theHazard: Field 2 of /proc/<pid>/stat is the executable name in parentheses and may itself contain spaces and ')' characters. A reader that splits the line on whitespace and takes the twenty-second token therefore lands on field 22 only when the process name is free of both. The safe formulation is positional counting after the last ')' in the line, which the contract does not state.
measurement.theContractForbidsThisStyle: linux.token still reads 'the first field after the "-" separator in that selected record (fs_vfstype). Not a numeric field ordinal.' That sentence exists because CLAUDE-V7-ADV-4 raised the identical hazard for mountinfo and v8 fixed it by citing the separator instead. v11 reintroduces the style it prohibits, on a file where the hazard is stronger than the one that prompted the prohibition.

shouldFix.consequence: This is the defence the whole PID-reuse repair exists to provide, and a mis-parse degrades it in both directions. If the misread token is a monotonically changing field such as utime or stime, the mandatory before-and-after comparison fails on every run and the profile refuses spuriously. If it is a static field, the comparison always succeeds and PID reuse goes undetected — the exact case CLAUDE-V10-S2 and PTCB-V10-S3 asked to be closed. Both readers apply the same wrong parse consistently, so nothing else in the contract catches it.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Cite the field the way the mountinfo token is cited: the twenty-second whitespace-separated field counted after the final ')' on the line, and say that a numeric ordinal counted from the start of the line is not the comparison. The macOS side needs no change — sysctl kern.proc.pid with kp_proc.p_starttime is a named structure field, not an ordinal.

coordinatorNote: v11 is the third consecutive generation with no blockers, and the repairs are increasingly precise rather than increasingly wordy: the tree-root serialization, the {pid, starttime} pair with a mandatory verification window on both platforms, the /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt inode with inode equality, the macOS declaration that the field is simply absent, and six retained fields that finally make the exact-volume and retargeting rules provable from a qualification trace. My own CLAUDE-V10-S1 is answered in the direction I asked and with the inventory-authorship collision handled head-on. Two things hold it. The first is the tail of that same finding: having decided the field lives on the carrier, the artifact left /tcbCarrier byte-identical and off the roster, so the carrier's own description still names one field with one author and knows nothing of this one — and PTCB-V3-S1 was raised on exactly that shape. The lineage's own remedy for 'named but not provisioned' is on record twice in the last two generations, and it was not applied here. The second is narrower and, I think, the sharper of the two: starttime is cited as '/proc/<pid>/stat field 22'. That file's second field is a parenthesised process name that may contain spaces and close-parens, so a positional split lands on field 22 only for well-behaved names, and the failure is silent in the dangerous direction — a static misread field makes the before-and-after comparison always succeed and the PID-reuse defence inert. The contract already forbids this citation style in the sentence next door, for the mountinfo token, after I raised the same hazard at v7; the fix is to count after the final close-paren and say so. Both advisories concern the honesty apparatus rather than the design: two of the three items in Codex's PTCB-V10-A1 are unrepaired while the log claims that finding addressed, and the log claims a spelling repair that the note it authored this generation does not have. DR-126 stays OPEN, no row of any number is marked SATISFIED, all five D-096 occurrences are prohibitions, no per-OS table is populated, and nothing here qualifies G22 or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. The subject, prompt, file 08 and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md were not edited and nothing was committed.
